A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Neuro-3D and the EEG-3D dataset. Their text, equations, tables and figures are readable and match reliably. v1 ends with references; v3 additionally contains supplementary Sections 7–11, which were included in the comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original EEG recordings from 12 participants, classification and reconstruction results, ablations, and brain-region analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains the original empirical results and additionally reports geometric reconstruction scores, individual-subject results and reconstruction failure cases.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the same attention-based dynamic–static EEG fusion, decoupled geometry and appearance features, training objectives, and two-stage shape/color decoder. The method text and Equations (1)–(12) are unchanged apart from citations and formatting.

E1.justification: Both versions use EEG-3D with the same 12 participants, 72 object categories, six color categories, and static-image and rotating-video stimuli. The supplementary analyses concern this existing dataset and its retained classification and reconstruction tasks.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains DeepNet, EEGNet, Conformer and TSConv. Table 4 retains Static, Dynamic, Concat and the variant without feature decoupling. The newly identified PointNet++ model serves as an evaluator, not an added competing reconstruction method.

E3.justification: v3 adds Chamfer Distance, scaled by 10^-2, and F1 score (%) to the reconstruction evaluation, displayed under the best-of-five heading in Table 4. Existing splits, training settings and semantic metrics remain unchanged. Supplementary preprocessing and five-subject evaluation details are new disclosures rather than evidence of revised settings.

E4.justification: The supplement substantially expands the analyses with classification performance across all 12 individuals (Section 9, Figure 6) and an explicit study of fine-detail failures versus semantic reconstruction errors (Section 11, Figure 8). Table 4 also extends the existing component ablations to geometric fidelity; the original ablations and brain-region analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report average and best performance over five generated samples. v3 adds no new run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Figure 6 shows differences between participants rather than uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 2–3 and the original semantic-score columns of Table 4 are unchanged. v3 adds substantial evidence on geometry and variability: Full achieves CD 5.35 and F1 77.01, versus Static 6.75/67.61 and Dynamic 6.40/69.42, alongside individual-subject scores and additional successful and failed reconstructions. These are newly reported outcomes, not performance gains between versions.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, attention formulation, losses and diffusion derivation in Equations (1)–(12) are retained. No new assumptions, proofs or formal results accompany the added empirical metrics.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims: introducing EEG-based colored 3D decoding, the EEG-3D dataset, and the fusion encoder with a two-stage decoder. The additional evidence does not redefine or broaden these contributions.

C2.justification: Section 5.3.1 now interprets dynamic EEG's better geometric scores as evidence of richer depth and shape information. The supplement adds interpretations of task-dependent individual differences and attributes reconstruction failures to EEG noise and limited spatial resolution. The existing texture-generation and cross-subject limitations remain.

D1.justification: Sections 7–8 newly document MNE preprocessing, epoch lengths, resampling, filters, normalization and trial averaging. They also identify PointNet++, explain evaluator training and test-set exclusion, disclose reconstruction evaluation on the first five subjects, and clarify sample selection. The abstract replaces a future-release promise with a stated code/data repository; its availability was not checked externally.

R1.justification: v3 adds nine references covering MNE, normalization, PointNet++, event-related potentials, individual EEG variability and visual-decoding reviews. The central positioning relative to 2D decoding and fMRI-based 3D reconstruction remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most prose remain intact. Changes include local wording and paragraph adjustments, expanded Section 3.3, updated authors and affiliations, acknowledgments, and supplementary Sections 7–11. There is no extensive rewrite of the existing narrative.

P2.justification: v3 adds individual-subject radar plots, a large reconstruction gallery and a failure-case figure (Figures 6–8), and expands Table 4 with geometric columns. Figure 4 is moved and resized. The supplementary gallery combines reused examples with additional reconstructions; the original figures' scientific content is retained.

improvement.justification: v1 evaluates reconstruction quantitatively through semantic classification and leaves essential EEG preprocessing and evaluator details unspecified. v3 substantially reduces these gaps through direct geometric evaluation in Table 4 and reproducibility information in Sections 7–8. Individual-subject results and explicit failure cases also make the evidence more transparent and qualify the successful examples, materially strengthening assessment of the unchanged method.
